questions.question: What encoder-decoder design premise distinguishes this work from many segmentation systems?

options.A: A generic task-independent VGG10 encoder is shared, while decoder design is optimized for segmentation
options.B: A segmentation-specific dilated encoder is paired with a generic classifier decoder
options.C: Separate encoders are trained for every output class and combined by a CRF
options.D: The encoder is removed and all pixel labels are predicted by a shallow FCN

questions.rationale: The authors assume the multi-task system has an efficient shared encoder and concentrate on a lightweight segmentation decoder.
questions.evidence_quote: we focus on efﬁcient design of the segmentation decoder and assume that an efﬁcient encoder is already designed

questions.question: Why does the proposed non-bottleneck block use multiple skip connections?

options.A: To distribute high gradients over multiple paths during back-propagation in a relatively shallow network
options.B: To pass max-pooling indices from every encoder stage into the decoder
options.C: To eliminate batch normalization from all convolutional layers
options.D: To reduce the number of feature maps from 256 directly to four

questions.rationale: The authors argue shallow residual networks can have difficulty handling high gradient flow; parallel skips distribute it.
questions.evidence_quote:
the incoming gradient gets dis-
tributed among all paths.

questions.question: What is the key architectural difference between the two proposed non-bottleneck variants?

options.A: Type-2 uses dilated 3×3 and 5×5 convolutions, whereas type-1 does not
options.B: Type-1 uses only 1×1 kernels, whereas type-2 uses only deconvolutions
options.C: Type-2 omits all skip connections and batch normalization
options.D: Type-1 is dilated and type-2 uses only 1D convolutions

questions.rationale: The variant distinction is dilation in the block on the right; the paper holds dilation rate at one for this study.
questions.evidence_quote:
The only difference between two
variants is the block at the right uses dilated convo-
lution where the kernel size is 3X3 and 5X5.

questions.question: Why did the authors avoid increasing the decoder's width after the encoder reduces its feature maps from 256 to four?

options.A: A wider decoder would substantially increase runtime beyond the embedded budget
options.B: Four channels are mathematically required for deconvolution
options.C: The training labels contain only two classes
options.D: The encoder outputs no intermediate feature maps to fuse

questions.rationale: The study prioritizes execution speed under automotive resource constraints, so increasing decoder width is considered unaffordable.
questions.evidence_quote: if we make the decoder wider that will shoot up the runtime signiﬁcantly.

questions.question: Which deconvolution and skip-fusion choices characterize the decoder described in Section 3.1?

options.A: It reconstructs with deconvolution and consumes final plus intermediate encoder feature maps
options.B: It uses max-unpooling only and passes no intermediate encoder maps
options.C: It uses a fully connected layer to restore the original image dimensions
options.D: It upsamples by nearest-neighbor interpolation and concatenates raw RGB input

questions.rationale: The decoder takes last-layer and intermediate features and uses deconvolution rather than SegNet-style max-unpooling.
questions.evidence_quote: For reconstruction we use deconvolution layer instead max-unpooling as used in SegNet

questions.question: How is the task dataset divided, and which four semantic classes are evaluated?

options.A: 3016 training, 981 validation, 1002 test images; lanes, curb, road, and void
options.B: 3016 training, 1002 validation, 981 test images; cars, pedestrians, road, and sky
options.C: 981 training, 3016 validation, 1002 test images; lanes, curb, road, and vehicles
options.D: 4000 training, 500 validation, 499 test images; road, sidewalk, signs, and buildings

questions.rationale: The dataset section gives the split sizes and defines void as everything else alongside the three driving-critical classes.
questions.evidence_quote: The entire dataset is divided into Training, Validation and Test set each containing 3016, 981 and 1002 images respectively.

questions.question: What training choices were used for optimization and data augmentation?

options.A: Adam, batch size 4, initial learning rate 0.0005 with polynomial decay over 350K iterations, and no augmentation
options.B: SGD, batch size 8, constant learning rate 0.01, and random crops/flips
options.C: Adam, batch size 32, cosine decay over 35K iterations, and heavy color augmentation
options.D: RMSProp, batch size 4, no pretraining, and synthetic data only

questions.rationale: The training description specifies Adam, batch size four, the initial learning rate and polynomial schedule; no data augmentation was performed.
questions.evidence_quote:
Training was started with 0.0005
as initial learning rate including standard polynomial
decay strategy to decrease this value over 350K itera-
tions.

questions.question: Which reported optimal-decoder IoU values correspond to lanes, curb, road, and mean?
questions.rationale: These are the table's Optimal row values; the other options correspond to named decoder variants.

questions.question: What runtime trade-off and class-specific gains do the authors report for the optimal decoder?

options.A: Less than 2 ms extra runtime over FCN, with 12% and 18% higher IoU for lanes and curb
options.B: More than 20 ms extra runtime, with 12% and 18% lower IoU for lanes and curb
options.C: No runtime increase, with 10% improvements only for road and void
options.D: Less than 2 ms extra runtime, with 18% and 12% gains for road and curb

questions.rationale: The conclusion says the key classes lanes and curb improved 12% and 18%; comparison with FCN cost under 2 ms runtime.
questions.evidence_quote: with less than 2ms increase in runtime.

questions.question: What limitation/next step do the authors explicitly identify after their decoder comparison?

options.A: Their study is preliminary; they propose fixed-runtime meta-architectures with optimal configurations learned by meta-learning
options.B: The dataset is too large for embedded systems, so they propose replacing segmentation with classification
options.C: The VGG10 encoder is already task-specific, so future work will remove the decoder
options.D: The method requires extensive data augmentation, so future work will avoid validation

questions.rationale: They frame the work as preliminary and propose learning a family of fixed-runtime meta-architectures in future work.
